main_issue: Who covers or completes Agent D's half-done analysis section before Thursday's deadline, given D's bereavement; D ends up agreeing to finish it tonight.

A-B.evidence: A asked for someone to take over D's section and then pressed D to deliver tonight (T3, T9); B refused to take it on (T4) and questioned D doing it tonight (T10). They never directly addressed each other, but their positions are somewhat opposed.

A-C.evidence: A asked for someone to get up to speed (T3); C declined (T5). Neither addressed the other afterward, and C never commented on D's tonight plan.

A-D.evidence: A rejected D's 'tomorrow night' plan (T7) and D agreed: 'I can finish it tonight' (T8). A thanked D (T9), and D held to the plan (T12).

B-C.evidence: Both declined to take on D's section (T4, T5). Neither spoke to the other.

B-D.evidence: B questioned whether D should work tonight (T10); D said they would do it after being with family (T12); B accepted ('Okay, Agent D', T13) and D thanked B (T14). B showed reluctance but did not oppose.

C-D.evidence: C declined the work (T5) and D said 'I understand' (T6), but C never addressed D's final plan, so the relation is unclear.
